qt: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:

The unexplained death of a woman employed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Russia in October 2026 has raised questions about biosecurity and the independent investigation of possible lab incidents. Although no link with the plague has been confirmed, the case highlights the importance of transparent safety standards for research involving particularly dangerous pathogens. 1.

What criteria does the Commission apply when backing or supporting research projects involving particularly dangerous pathogens, in order to make sure that the anticipated health benefits justify the risks to workers and the general public, and how is that assessment independently verified?
How does the Commission make sure that high-risk EU-funded research projects have explored lower-risk alternatives?

What measures is it taking to monitor compliance with EU biosecurity requirements where research involves hazardous pathogens, and is it advocating at international level for independent security checks and transparent reporting requirements in the case of lab incidents?
